question: A 4-year-old boy presents with recurrent liver abscesses and lymphadenitis caused by Staphylococcus aureus and Aspergillus fumigatus. His absolute lymphocyte count and immunoglobulin levels are normal. The nitroblue tetrazolium (NBT) test shows no colour change. What is the most likely diagnosis?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. CGD results from a defect in NADPH oxidase — the enzyme phagocytes use to generate superoxide for the oxidative (respiratory) burst. Catalase-positive organisms (S. aureus, Aspergillus, Serratia, Burkholderia) neutralise their own H₂O₂ and therefore depend entirely on the phagocyte's oxidative burst for killing. The NBT test confirms the absent burst — normal neutrophils reduce NBT to blue formazan, while CGD neutrophils cannot.

Incorrect. XLA (Bruton's disease) features absent B cells and immunoglobulins, causing recurrent pyogenic sinopulmonary infections after 6 months when maternal IgG wanes. This child has normal immunoglobulin levels, ruling out XLA. The abnormal NBT test points specifically to a phagocyte oxidative burst defect — chronic granulomatous disease.

Incorrect. DiGeorge syndrome (thymic aplasia, 22q11 deletion) causes T-cell deficiency with recurrent viral and fungal infections, along with hypocalcaemia from parathyroid agenesis. This child has normal lymphocyte counts, and the combination of catalase-positive organisms with an abnormal NBT test indicates a phagocyte disorder (CGD), not T-cell deficiency.

Incorrect. SCID causes profound T and B cell deficiency with life-threatening infections in early infancy, failure to thrive, and absent lymphoid tissue. This child has normal lymphocytes and immunoglobulins, which rules out SCID. The recurrent catalase-positive organism infections and abnormal NBT test are diagnostic of CGD — a phagocyte disorder.

overallFeedback.feedback: Key clue: normal lymphocytes and immunoglobulins rule out B cell, T cell, and combined deficiencies. The abnormal NBT test identifies a phagocyte oxidative burst defect (CGD), and catalase-positive organisms are the clinical signature.
Well done! CGD with an abnormal NBT test and recurrent catalase-positive organism infections is a classic diagnostic triad in primary immunodeficiency.
